skills.description: Use ACE-Step API to generate music, edit songs, and remix music. Supports text-to-music, lyrics generation, audio continuation, and audio repainting. Use this skill when users mention generating music, creating songs, music production, remix, or audio continuation.

ACE-Step documentation and troubleshooting. Use when users ask about installing ACE-Step, GPU configuration, model download, Gradio UI usage, API integration, or troubleshooting issues like VRAM problems, CUDA errors, or model loading failures.

Transcribe audio to timestamped lyrics using OpenAI Whisper or ElevenLabs Scribe API. Outputs LRC, SRT, or JSON with word-level timestamps. Use when users want to transcribe songs, generate LRC files, or extract lyrics with timestamps from audio.

Render music videos from audio files and lyrics using Remotion. Accepts audio + LRC/JSON lyrics + title to produce MP4 videos with waveform visualization and synced lyrics display. Use when users mention MV generation, music video rendering, creating video from audio/lyrics, or visualizing songs.

Music songwriting guide for ACE-Step. Provides professional knowledge on writing captions, lyrics, choosing BPM/key/duration, and structuring songs. Use this skill when users want to create, write, or plan a song before generating it with ACE-Step.

Generate song cover/thumbnail images using Gemini API. Creates artistic images suitable for music video backgrounds. Use when users want to generate album art, song covers, thumbnails, or background images for MVs.
Provides information about the bitwize-music plugin, its version, and its creator. Use when the user asks about the plugin, its purpose, version, or capabilities.
Creates visual concepts for album artwork and generates AI art prompts. Use during planning for concept discussion, or after all tracks are Final for actual artwork generation.
Designs album concepts, tracklist architecture, and thematic planning through 7 structured phases. Use when planning a new album or reworking an existing album concept.
Shows a structured progress dashboard for an album with percentage complete per phase, blocking items, and status breakdown. Use for a quick visual overview of album progress.
Tracks and manages album ideas including brainstorming, planning, and status updates. Use when the user wants to add, review, or organize their album idea backlog.
Copies track content (lyrics, style prompts, streaming lyrics) to the system clipboard. Use when the user needs to paste lyrics or style prompts into Suno or other external tools.
Uploads promo videos and content to Cloudflare R2 or AWS S3. Use when the user wants to host promo content for social media or distribution.
Sets up or edits the plugin configuration file interactively. Use on first-time setup, when config is missing, or when the user wants to change settings.

Searches and retrieves documents from free public sources using automated browser navigation. Use when research needs primary source documents like court filings, government reports, or public records.
Scans lyrics for explicit content and verifies that explicit flags match actual content. Use before Suno generation or release to ensure accurate content ratings.

Create new genre documentation files for the bitwize-music genre library. Use when the user wants to add a genre, says "/genre-creator", "neues Genre erstellen", "Genre hinzufuegen", "add genre", or asks to create genre documentation. Takes a genre name as argument.
Runs plugin health checks (venv packages, skill registration, and album slug collisions). Use when the user asks to check plugin health, verify setup, or troubleshoot missing skills.
Shows available skills, common workflows, and quick reference for the plugin. Use when the user asks for help, what skills are available, or how to do something.
Places album art files in the correct audio and content directory locations. Use when the user has generated or downloaded album artwork that needs to be saved.
Moves audio files to the correct album location with proper path structure. Use when the user has downloaded WAV files from Suno or other sources that need to be organized.
Moves track markdown files to the correct album location. Use when the user has track files in Downloads or other locations that need to be placed in an album.
Autonomous multi-pass lyric refinement for tightening, cohesion, and album unity. Use after lyrics are written to polish a track or entire album through iterative passes.
Reviews lyrics against a quality checklist before Suno generation. Use before generating tracks to catch rhyme, prosody, pronunciation, and structural issues.
Writes or reviews lyrics with professional prosody, rhyme craft, and quality checks. Use when writing new lyrics, revising existing lyrics, or when the user says 'let's work on a track.
Guides audio mastering for streaming platforms including loudness optimization and tonal balance. Use when the user has approved tracks and wants to master audio files.

Polishes raw Suno audio by processing per-stem WAVs (vocals, backing_vocals, drums, bass, guitar, keyboard, strings, brass, woodwinds, percussion, synth, other) with targeted cleanup, EQ, and compression, then remixing into a polished stereo WAV ready for mastering. Use after audio import and before mastering.
Creates a new album with the correct directory structure and templates. Use IMMEDIATELY when the user says 'make a new album' or similar, before any discussion.
Analyzes album state and recommends the optimal next action. Use when the user asks "what should I do next?" or "what's left to do?
Scans lyrics for phrases that may match existing songs using web search and LLM knowledge. Use before release to check for unintentional borrowing.

Validates all pre-generation gates before sending tracks to Suno. Checks sources verified, lyrics reviewed, pronunciation resolved, explicit flag set, style prompt complete, and artist names cleared. Use before generating tracks on Suno or when the user says "pre-gen check" or "ready to generate".
Generates 15-second vertical promo videos for social media from mastered audio. Use after mastering is complete and before release, when the user wants social media content.
Reviews and iterates on social media copy in album promo/ files. Use after populating promo templates and before release to polish platform-specific posts.
Generates platform-specific social media copy from album themes, track concepts, and lyrics. Use when promo/ templates need to be populated before release.
Converts an album idea from IDEAS.md into an actual album project in one step. Use when the user says "promote [idea title]", "turn idea into album", or "start working on [idea]".
Scans lyrics for pronunciation risks and prevents Suno mispronunciations. Use when writing lyrics with proper nouns, technical terms, homographs, or non-English words.
Coordinates album release including QA, distribution prep, and platform uploads. Use when mastering and album art are complete and the user is ready to release.
Renames an album or track, updating slugs, titles, and all mirrored paths. Use when the user wants to rename an album or track.
Conducts investigative-grade research with primary source analysis, cross-verification, and trial-level depth. Use when an album needs factual research, source material, or verification of claims.
Researches personal backgrounds, interviews, motivations, and humanizing details. Use when research needs biographical context about people involved in the album's subject.
Researches SEC filings, earnings calls, analyst reports, and market data. Use when the album subject involves financial crimes, corporate stories, or market events.
Researches DOJ/FBI/SEC press releases, agency statements, and government sources. Use when research needs official government records or agency documentation.
Researches archives, contemporary accounts, and timeline reconstruction. Use when the album subject involves historical events that need primary source verification.
Researches investigative articles, interviews, and news coverage. Use when research needs journalistic sources for cross-referencing or additional context.
Researches court documents, indictments, plea agreements, and sentencing records. Use when the album subject involves legal proceedings or criminal cases.
Researches the subject's own words from tweets, blogs, forums, and chat logs. Use when research needs direct quotes or first-person accounts.
Researches malware analysis, CVEs, attribution reports, and hacker community sources. Use when the album subject involves cybersecurity incidents or threat actors.
Researches project histories, changelogs, developer interviews, and open source documentation. Use when the album subject involves technology projects or developer stories.
Performs quality control, citation validation, and fact-checking before human review. Use after research is complete to verify all sources and claims before production.
Finds an album by name and shows detailed status with next steps. Use when the user mentions an album name or wants to continue previous work.
Runs the session startup procedure - verifies setup, loads config and state, checks skill models, and reports project status. Use at the beginning of a fresh session.
Detects your Python environment and guides you through installing plugin dependencies. Use on first-time setup or when MCP server fails to start.
Converts mastered audio to sheet music and creates printable songbooks. Use after mastering when the user wants sheet music or a songbook for their album.

Constructs technical Suno style prompts for the current model family (v6, v6-wild, v6-mini), selects models and generation settings, and optimizes prompts. Use when creating or refining Suno prompts for track generation.
Runs automated tests to validate plugin integrity across 14 categories. Use before creating PRs, after making changes to skills or templates, or to verify plugin health.
Provides interactive guided album creation for new users. Use when the user is new to the plugin or asks for a walkthrough of the album creation process.
Validates album directory structure, file locations, and content integrity. Use before release or whenever the user wants to check an album's structural health.
Captures human source verification for tracks, timestamps it, and updates track files. Use when sources need human review before generation.

Reviews lyrics and prose for AI-written patterns (abstract noun stacking, over-explained metaphors, cliche escalation, missing idiosyncrasy, prose AI tells). Advisory Warning/Info severity — flags issues, does not block or rewrite. Use when reviewing lyrics for authenticity or before generation to catch AI-sounding language.

Use when the user has a Session-view loop and wants to promote it to a full Arrangement, build sections (intro/verse/drop/break/outro), or extend a 4-bar idea into a 3-minute track. Examples - "turn this loop into a full song", "build me a 2-minute arrangement from this", "promote session to arrangement".

Use when the user wants to generate, voice, or modify chord progressions. Examples - "give me a sad chord progression in C minor", "voice these chords for piano", "what's a good progression for cinematic music?", "extend this progression with more color tones".

Use when the user wants drum patterns by genre - kick, snare, hi-hat, percussion. Examples - "give me a trap beat", "house drum pattern", "DnB drums at 174", "lo-fi drums with swing", "boom-bap pattern".

Use when the user is finishing a track and wants to check it's ready to send to a mastering engineer or for self-mastering. Audits headroom, peak levels, mono compatibility, frequency balance, LUFS. Examples - "is this ready to master?", "audit my mix before export", "check my levels".

Use when the user asks to humanize a MIDI part, fix voice leading, quantize notes, clean up timing, fix stuck/duplicate notes, or generally polish a MIDI clip they recorded or wrote. Examples - "humanize this hat", "voice these chords better", "the timing is too stiff", "fix the voice leading on the strings".

Use when the user describes a mix problem ("muddy", "harsh", "no headroom", "vocals get lost", "kick and bass fighting") or asks for a mix audit. Diagnoses the issue from session state and proposes specific corrective moves with EQ, compression, sends, and routing.

Use when the user asks to set up tracks, pick instruments, scaffold an arrangement, build a project template, or describe a track they want to make in Ableton Live. Examples - "make me a 4-bar lo-fi loop", "set up a film score template", "I want to start a hip-hop beat in C minor".

Use when the user references another track they want to emulate the vibe/sound of. Examples - "make this sound like Ólafur Arnalds", "I want a Tame Impala vibe", "match the mix of Kendrick's Money Trees". Translates artist/track references into actionable production decisions.

Use when the user wants to set up sidechain compression - typically kick → bass, kick → pads, vocals → music bed. Examples - "sidechain my bass to the kick", "make the synths duck under the vocal", "add pumping to the chords".

Use when the user wants to design a synth patch from scratch or modify an existing one - lead, bass, pad, pluck, lush keys, FX. Targets stock Ableton synths (Operator, Wavetable, Analog, Drift). Examples - "make me a wide supersaw lead", "design a sub bass", "give me a lush pad like Olafur Arnalds".

Use when the user is unsure about tempo, time signature, or rhythmic feel choices. Examples - "what tempo should this be?", "should I switch to 3/4?", "is 95 BPM right for lo-fi?", "how do I make this feel less stiff rhythmically?".

Use when the user has recorded vocals and wants a processing chain set up. Examples - "set up my vocal chain", "process this vocal", "make the vocal sit in the mix", "give me a pop vocal chain", "make this rap vocal aggressive".

The pre-delivery AI-tell audit for lyrics (歌词 AI 味诊断). Run this on every draft before it ships. The eight enumerable symptoms that make AI-written lyrics recognisable in one listen, which are machine-countable and which need a person, the diagnostic path from symptom to owning skill, why a draft that passes every check can still be lifeless, and the remediation list. Use when a lyric draft is about to be delivered, when a draft reads fine but feels generic, when deciding whether to accept a version, or when a lyric passed LYR-LINT but still sounds machine-written. AI 味、歌词诊断、验收、太泛、像 AI 写的、交稿前检查。

The Cantonese layer for lyric writing (粤语填词的协音层). Cantonese has nine tones plus a tenth, and a syllable sung against its own tone is heard as a different word, so tone-melody agreement is a hard constraint, not a risk score. Gives the worked system; the nine tone values and their singing names 「三九四〇五二一八六」, the four class-scales 「〇二四三」 grouping the tones by tone-tail, the truth table of natural intervals between adjacent characters, true values versus approximations and best approximation, the three-eighths and three-sixteenths laws, the elasticity of natural intervals (outward-stretching versus inward-drawn classes, the ring diagram, crossing the boundary means a wrong tone), the six-tone same-rhyme test, and when a title line may deliberately be sung off. Also covers melody-first order, rhyme, the entering tone, register, and style periods. Use when writing or checking Cantonese lyrics, or when a sung line comes out as the wrong word. 粤语、协音、九声、类音阶、声调唱名、真值表、自然音距、最佳逼近、八分三定律、六调试音法、粤语歌填词、旋律先定、入声。

The case layer - how to take a finished lyric apart and what three working lyricists say about their own habits (案例与拆解). A fixed twelve-row worksheet for dissecting any song, keyed to the library's own fields so every finding lands in a skill instead of staying an impression; the rule that a real lyric is read from the middle outward, not from the theme down; what Yao Qian, Zhang Li and Hong Yuan each say about opening lines, restraint, revision, rhyme width, colloquial versus literary diction and how much to leave the composer, plus the four places they openly disagree and how to pick a side; worked dissections of songs the sources analyse in full, including one song two of them discuss independently; and the failure patterns they name - flat, scattered, overlong, bland, blunt, bare, stuffed. Use when studying a lyric you admire, when you need a real example of a technique, when a draft feels wrong and you want a model to compare against, or when asked to critique a song. 案例、拆解、词评、作品分析、词人自述、改稿对照。

The Chinese-style layer for lyric writing (中国风歌词). What makes a lyric read as 中国风 rather than merely decorated - the vocabulary families it draws on (place, dynasty, object, craft, plant), the sixteen rhetorical devices Fang Wen-shan catalogues inside his own lyrics, each with a book example and a failure condition, why every image must belong to one material world and how one out-of-period object breaks it, the four grades of borrowing from classical verse and where borrowing becomes copying, what to do when the listener will not catch the allusion, what the words promise the arrangement when they name an instrument, and the three ways this style usually dies - ornament with no event, images unrelated to what the song says, and archaism for its own sake. Use when writing or auditing a 中国风 or 古风 lyric, when a draft is full of beautiful old words but says nothing, when checking an allusion, when images from different eras collide, or when the words name an instrument. 中国风、古风、典故、化用、文字游戏、修辞、意象成套、方文山、穿帮。

The English language layer for lyric writing (英文词的重音与节拍对齐). Word stress is fixed inside a polysyllabic word, so the melody bends to the word and never the reverse; stressed syllables belong on stressed notes, which keeps the natural shape of the language; line length is counted in stressed syllables, not total syllables; common meter and its 4-3 stress lines; long syllables want long notes and the contour should track the sentence's intonation; where the breath falls, how phrase length accelerates a section, what enjambment costs; what gonna, wanna and 'em do to the count; why the, of and and must not land on a downbeat; and the mistakes a Chinese-speaking writer makes in English. Use when writing or checking English lyrics, fitting English words to a melody, when a sung line sounds mispronounced, when counting syllables, or when a line will not fit the bar. 英文作词、英文歌词、重音、节拍对齐、音节数、prosody、phrasing、气口、重音落错、唱不进小节。

The imagery layer - how to find concrete nouns and make them a system (意象与具体名词). Object writing and the seven senses, the ten-minute timed practice, why abstract nouns are the most direct AI fingerprint and how to build the forbidden list, how to check that a lyric is not all sight, why a set of images must belong to one physical world instead of being piled up at random, simile versus metaphor and how to spot and replace a dead one, and how one object recurs with a shifting meaning. Use when a lyric feels vague or generic but the words look fine, when every noun in a draft is a concept, when you cannot find images, when images are pretty but unrelated, when a metaphor sounds borrowed, or when LYR-LINT check 2 fails. 意象、具体名词、抽象词、object writing、物体写作、五感、七感、比喻、明喻、暗喻、通感、陈词、死喻、词太泛、找不到意象。

The Japanese language layer for lyric writing (日文词的モーラ与符割り). The counting unit is the mora, not the kana or the syllable - the small tsu, the moraic n and the long vowel each take a beat, a palatalized pair takes one; one kana per note is the default, and the same melody remaps itself when the words change; every word carries a pitch-accent contour, and a melody that fights it gets the line heard as a different sentence; fuwari, the mapping of kana to notes; bunsetsu segmentation and where a line may break; ji-amari and ji-tarazu as deliberate mismatch; the four ways to fix a melody when the counts do not fit; why Japanese rhyme is weak and how shichigo-cho slips in unnoticed; the lyrics-first and music-first routes; and the iron rule for English words inside a Japanese song. Use when writing or checking Japanese lyrics, fitting kana to an existing melody, counting morae, when a sung line is misheard as another word, or when the words will not sit on the notes. 日文作词、日语歌词、モーラ、拍数、符割り、字余り、字足らず、音高重音、七五調。

The Korean language layer for lyric writing (韩文词的音节与받침). One hangul block is one syllable is one note by default - unlike Japanese, a final consonant takes no beat of its own. The batchim (받침, syllable-final consonant) is the subject here; single and double batchim, the seven representative finals, and why a syllable closing on a stop is the wrong place for a long note, a phrase-end hold or a section peak. Liaison (연음) moves a batchim onto the next block, so the sung syllable boundary is not the written one, which moves every breath, caesura and rhyme landing. Plus the sound changes that rewrite a line between paper and voice (nasalization, tensification, aspiration, palatalization, elision, insertion, vowel harmony); why Korean has no tone and no word stress; how Korean rhyme differs from the Mandarin che. Use when writing or checking Korean lyrics, fitting hangul to a melody, counting syllables, or picking a word for a held note. 韩文作词、韩语歌词、받침、收音、连音、音变、音节数、K-pop 填词。

The Mandarin language layer for lyric writing (普通话作词的语言层). What Chinese as a language adds to the job; tone is phonemic, so the melody that enters a syllable can change which word is heard; one character is one syllable, so syllable count is character count; the thirteen rhyme families (十三辙) with their finals, example characters, wide-versus-narrow reach and loudness grades; how to pick a rhyme family, when to switch, and which families borrow from each other; level-and-oblique (平仄) and how much looser a lyric is than classical verse; the two- and three-character feet that make a Chinese line scan; and what makes a line easy or hard to sing. Use when writing or checking Mandarin lyrics, when choosing or changing a rhyme family, when a line is a tongue-twister or a high note lands on a closed vowel, when someone asks what 十三辙 is, or when LYR-LINT check 8 says the song sits on one or two wide families. 普通话、中文作词、十三辙、辙口、韵部、平仄、字调、易唱、绕口、开口音闭口音、什么是十三辙。

Theatre and musical-theatre lyric writing (剧场与音乐剧唱词). How a song becomes an action instead of a pause, how to make the words sound like the character rather than the lyricist, and what Sondheim's three principles - Content Dictates Form, Less Is More, God Is in the Details, all in the service of clarity - actually change in a draft. Covers character diction by vocabulary, syntax, schooling and period; first-person versus narrator; the price of repetition and the function of perfect rhyme on a stage; the seam between song and dialogue; Sondheim's catalogue of his own faults; and a transfer table for which rules a pop lyric should also obey. Use when writing a song for a character in a play or musical, when a song feels like a pause in the story, when two characters sound alike, when turning a scene into a song, or when deciding whether a theatre rule applies to a pop lyric. 音乐剧、剧场、角色唱词、戏剧、推进剧情、Sondheim、唱词与对白。

Who is speaking, when they are speaking, and how much they are allowed to know (歌词的叙事层). The three narrative fields every lyric must fill - point of view, tense anchor, and the one thing deliberately left unsaid - with the cost of each person, the risk of mixing pronouns mid-song and the few shifts that actually work, how present/past/future change the listener's distance, why a fixed moment limits what the speaker can know (write the symptom, not the conclusion), why a completed emotional arc (hurt - peace - blessing) is a machine fingerprint, and how a story lyric advances through scene, turn and cost. Use when a draft has no speaker, when you cannot tell who is being addressed, when pronouns drift between sections, when the timeline is half memory and half now, when a lyric resolves everything and leaves nothing hanging, when writing a story song, or when LYR-LINT check 5 or 6 fails. 视角、人称、时间、时态、留白、不解决、叙事、故事型歌词、没有说话人、谁在说话、情绪走完整。

Writing the words of a rap (说唱的词本身), not how the vocal sits in the beat. Rhyme density - how many rhymed syllables per bar and what it costs in intelligibility; multisyllable and compound rhymes, assonance, consonance, bent words, internal rhyme; rhyme schemes from couplet to whole-verse and where the rhyme lands; content forms (braggadocio, battle, concept, story, abstract, humorous) and line-level tools (punchline, wordplay, double meaning, simile, extended analogy); vocabulary, slang and its shelf life, rhyme-driven versus meaning-driven writing; the writing order MCs actually use (flow first or words first, freestyle, editing); and a transfer table for Mandarin rap, where one character is one syllable and every syllable carries a tone. Use when writing a rap verse or hook, turning an existing lyric into rap, when rhymes feel thin or predictable, when a verse rhymes well but says nothing, or when adapting English rap technique to Chinese. 说唱、rap、押韵密度、多音节韵、内韵、punchline、flow、中文说唱、改成说唱、韵脚、battle、叙事说唱。

Rhyme as a structural tool, not decoration (押韵与韵式). The full stability scale from perfect rhyme through family, additive, subtractive, assonance, consonance and partial rhyme - what each type does to closure - how to place stable and unstable types in the pushing and resolving positions of a scheme, the characters of AABB, ABAB, ABCB and xaxa, the three closure types, internal and multisyllabic rhyme, how to widen a candidate list past the first word that comes to mind, and when to deliberately break the rhyme. Use when choosing rhyme words, when a section closes too hard or refuses to close, when every rhyme sounds like the obvious one, when picking a rhyme scheme for a verse or a chorus, or when the surprise check on rhyme words comes back low. 押韵、韵脚、家族韵、内韵、韵式、押韵太顺、破韵、故意不押、押不上、韵脚太熟。

The gate you must pass before writing a single line (动笔前必填). Five questions that force an actual choice - which kind of song this is (attitudinal, situational, narrative, or expository, and why the default is not narrative), the one thing it says, who it is said to, at what moment, and the one photographable object that runs through it - with the failure mode each question catches, the downstream choices the song type fixes (person, voice, repetition budget), how to tell a real answer from a filled-in one, and why this gate exists at all (AI-written lyrics are not bad at words, they are written by nobody). Use when starting any lyric, when a draft feels generic but you cannot say why, when every song comes out as a story, when a song is trying to say two things, or when LYR-LINT check 1 fails. 立意、动笔前必填、歌的类型、态度型、情境型、叙事型、说理型、只说一件事、对谁说、锚定物件、重复预算、写不出来、太泛。

The structural layer of a lyric (词的结构层) - what each section is for and what it must not say, which song form to pick, where the title lands and how often it comes back, and how line counts, line lengths and rhyme placement make a section feel finished or still owing something. Covers verse / pre-chorus / chorus / bridge / refrain functions, central versus developmental sections, AABA and verse-chorus and verse-refrain forms, the five structural parameters (balance, pace, flow, closure, closure type), the five hook-placement strategies, and the deliberate asymmetry that keeps a lyric from sounding machine-made. Use when laying out sections before writing a line, when a chorus does not feel like an arrival, when a bridge sounds like one more verse, when every section came out the same length, when deciding where the title goes, or when LYR-LINT check 3, 4 or 10 fails. 段落结构、曲式、副歌、bridge、hook、标题位置、句式、不对称、段落功能、AABA。

The tone-melody conflict detector and how to read it (倒字检测器). The one objective, computable criterion this library has - Mandarin dao-zi, where a syllable is heard as a different word because the melody enters it against its tone contour. Covers the correct model (incoming interval versus the syllable's own contour, not previous-end versus next-start), how to check it by hand, how to read a risk score, the three boundaries that make it a risk indicator rather than a verdict, and the five ways to fix a flagged syllable. Use when fitting Mandarin words to a melody, when a sung line is misheard as different words, when checking a draft before delivery, or when a melody must be adjusted to fit words already written. 倒字、依字行腔、字调、声调、检测器、唱出来听成了别的字、唱成别的字、字唱错了、tone_check。

Entry point and router for the lyric writing library (作词工作流与路由). The two workflows that fork at the very first question - music-first versus lyrics-first - and their different stage tables, which skill to load for which task, the full-library boundary table, the LYR-SPEC gate rules, the external interface (what the spec hands out, what it reads if present, the six fields shared with the music side, the messages channel), and three checks (requests that are easy to misroute, whether a draft can be told apart from human-written lyrics, the tone check). Load this FIRST for any lyric writing request, before deciding which other skill to read. Use when starting a lyric, when fitting words to an existing melody or a melody to existing words, when unsure which skill owns a question, when a draft fails lint, or when handing the lyric on to composition, recording or scoring. 作词、歌词、填词、工作流、路由、该读哪个 skill、LYR-SPEC、先曲后词、先词后曲。

The post-generation AI-tell audit (AI 味诊断). Run this on every generated track before accepting it. Covers the fourteen enumerable defaults that generative music models fall into, which of them are machine-measurable and which need ears, why compliance rate and AI-tell count are two separate numbers that must never be merged, the zero-point calibration that sets the pass threshold at 82 rather than 60, the ordered diagnostic path from symptom to owning skill, and the remediation list. Use when a generation comes back and must be accepted or rejected, when a track sounds synthetic but you cannot say why, when deciding whether to accept a take, or when a high compliance rate still produced a bad result. AI 味、诊断、验收、听不出来是 AI、照做率、生成后检查。

Arrangement architecture (编曲结构学) - the shape of a track over time rather than its notes. Energy curve and dramatic arc, subtractive arranging, layering as form (instrument entry/exit events), formal skeletons and section proportion, arrangement-hook placement, why the second verse must not be a copy, and how to end. Use when the user is arranging a song and asks how to structure it, when a track "goes nowhere" or "sounds flat", when every section sounds the same, when a generated track sounds like AI (monotonic energy, unchanging instrumentation, no subtraction), when deciding where instruments enter and leave, or when filling the arrangement/energy_curve/subtraction_events/roster fields of an ARR-SPEC. 编曲结构、能量曲线、减法、进退场、段落比例、钩子布局、结尾。

The corpus layer (语料层) - how real recordings are made to testify for or against the textbook rules. Covers the reverse ARR-SPEC as the unit of the corpus, the corroboration table that turns rules times corpus into hit rates and tiers them as strong rule / tendency / not a rule, the two honesty constraints that keep the table from being circular, why naturally sampled corpora beat curated ones, what this corpus can and cannot measure, and how to look up a worked example. Use when checking whether a rule actually holds in real music, when adding a rule, when a rule and the data disagree, when annotating a track, or when you need a real-world example of a technique. 语料、佐证、命中率、实测 ARR-SPEC、反向规格、案例拆解、规则验证。

Counterpoint and voice writing (对位与声部写作) - writing a second line that is genuinely independent rather than a harmony part. The four complementarity axes that make two lines combine (rhythmic density, interval colour, contrary/oblique/similar motion, staggered peaks), contrast between unlike versus like characters, the melodic constraints a contrapuntal line must obey, the five species, and invertible counterpoint for varying a repeat. Use when writing a counter-melody or obbligato, when checking voice leading in a multi-part passage (parallel fifths and octaves, hidden fifths, voice crossing and overlap), when two simultaneous lines sound glued together or fight, when a repeated section needs varying without new material, or when an arrangement is harmonically correct but flat. Not for ordinary bass or accompaniment writing. 对位、复调、副旋律、对旋律、声部独立、声部进行、平行五度、平行八度、隐伏五八度、声部交叉、四声部检查、二重对位、卡农。

Thematic development (乐思发展层) - what the theme is and what each section does with it. Owns `material` (motif, character, stated_in) and `form[].development`, a closed set of ten operations (repeat/sequence/extend/contract/fragment/vary/augment/counterpoint/new/recap). Covers the line between developing and piling up, each operation with its criterion and cost, motive-to-phrase construction, phrase-to-section-to-whole (overlap, supplement, recapitulation), the variation branch, and where it all lands in a pop song. Use when every section sounds like new material, when a song feels loose, when deciding what the second verse or the last chorus should do, or when filling `material` and `form[].development` in an ARR-SPEC. 乐思发展、动机、主题材料、每段都在写新东西、扩充、减缩、裁截、模进、变奏、再现。

Song form and section design (曲式与段落) - the terminology, the standard templates, and how to build a setsu backwards from the chorus. The Japanese section vocabulary mapped onto Anglo-American terms (and the two that are routinely mistranslated), the two broad families sorted by chorus position, the royal-road template with its repetition-omission rule, ternary form and the recapitulation principle, EDM and club variants, lead-in options, and the classical Chinese/Russian period-and-phrase apparatus for when pop terms run out. Use when laying out a song, when sections blur together, when deciding how many verse-chorus cycles, when a bridge is needed, or when filling the form table of an ARR-SPEC. 曲式、段落、结构、主歌副歌、桥段、乐段、再现、A メロ、サビ。

Functional and colour harmony (和声：功能与色彩) - choosing chords for a melody and then upgrading them without over-cooking. The three functions and three cadence types, the measure-by-measure harmonization procedure, substitution rules, seventh chords, and the colour techniques (slash chords, secondary dominants, two-fives, tritone substitution, subdominant minor, modal flavours, sus4, tensions, cliche lines, passing diminished, pedal point, blue notes) organised as a nine-step reharmonization checklist with an explicit stop rule. Use when harmonizing a melody, when a progression is bland or too busy, when a section needs a specific colour (wistful, jazzy, driving, chromatic bass), or when filling the harmony fields of an ARR-SPEC. 和声、和弦、配和声、终止式、重配和声、副属、二五、代理、张力音。

Melody writing (旋律法) - what a melodic line expresses and how to make it singable. Direction and interval width as expression, the hard limits on leaps and how to prepare and land them (windup, run-up, cushion, rebound), range setting against the human voice and the passaggio, long and short note values, cadence treatment and the eight degrees of closure, motive-phrase-section construction and the six causes of segmentation, and a checklist against predictable cliche. Use when writing or fixing a melody, when a line is unsingable or bland or too predictable, when deciding a key and range for a specific singer, when a melody gets buried by the accompaniment, or when filling melody_register in an ARR-SPEC. 旋律、曲调、跳进、音域、乐句、动机、唱不上去、太套路。

Mix intent as a handoff artifact (混音意图) - stating what a mix must achieve so a human engineer, a DAW, or a generative backend can all act on it, without prescribing EQ or compressor settings. The five domains (time, frequency, level, stereo, depth) and the imagined sound stage, the four goals (mood, balance, definition, interest), where balance is required and where depth must be consistent instead, the two legitimate reasons to be unbalanced, why sustained pads mask far more than short percussive hits, and how to use reference tracks as calibration. Use when writing the mix_intent block of an ARR-SPEC, handing a session to an engineer, deciding what a backend can actually honor, or diagnosing a mix that is technically clean but emotionally wrong. Grounded in masking (low masks high), critical bands, temporal masking, localization cues and the precedence effect. 混音意图、声场、掩蔽、临界频带、平衡、参考曲目、交接。

Modulation (转调) - moving between keys and making the seam sound intended rather than accidental. Closely related versus distant keys, the cushion chord and its announcement ladder from smoothest to most impactful, degree thinking, the three tools that keep a modulation feeling unified, what each interval distance expresses, a six-step decision flow including the return trip, and a warning about the one modulation generative models reach for by default. Use when a section needs to change key, when a key lift feels cheap or abrupt, when a modulation sounds accidental, when planning a bright-to-dark or dark-to-bright switch, or when returning to the home key. 转调、升key、离调、同主调、平行调、近亲调、远隔调、缓冲和弦。

Orchestration (配器) at the decision level - which instruments carry which line, pure vs mixed timbre, blending (unison, octave coupling, separate registers), balance, technique's effect on blend, register-dependent character, MIDI orchestration, and Chinese folk orchestra scoring - four sections, pairing/clash, melody/bass/harmony assignment, arranging/transplanting. Use when picking an instrument, adding a layer, muddy or vanishing woodwinds, fake MIDI mockups, erhu/pipa/dizi/suona/sheng/guzheng, or ARR-SPEC roster fields. 配器、乐器法、混合音色、八度叠合、乐器平衡、音区性格、MIDI 配器、民族管弦乐、民乐配器、二胡、琵琶、笛子、唢呐、笙、古筝、扬琴、总谱写法、移调乐器。 Tables in reference.md.

Chord progression lookup library (和弦进行速查库) - the eight famous named progressions with their variants and what each one actually does, a mood reverse-lookup, the eight variation techniques that turn one standard progression into ten, and an explicit warning list of the progressions generative models default to. This is a lookup skill, not a teaching skill - it answers "give me a progression that does X". Harmonizing a melody, choosing chords bar by bar, or reharmonizing is mc-harmony, and a full track needs mc-harmony first and this table second. Use when you need a progression for a specific mood or section, when a loop feels stale, when varying a standard progression, or when checking whether a progression is too defaulted-to. 和弦进行、王道进行、卡农、小室、丸サ、循环、套路、换个进行。

The compiler from ARR-SPEC to any generation backend (编译层). One compiler, many backends - the backend differences live in backends.yaml as data, never as separate skills. Covers the compile order, section-tag mapping, turning structured fields into prose style prompts without losing information, lyric chunking, the honors contract that decides which fields are scorable, degradation strategy when a backend cannot execute a field, seeds and best-of-N, and what to hand over so the user can run it in whatever tool hosts the backend. Use when turning a finished ARR-SPEC into Suno / YuE2 / MiniMax / ACE-Step / symbolic output, when choosing a backend, when a generation ignored the spec, or when adding a new backend. 编译、后端、Suno、YuE2、MiniMax、ACE-Step、提示词生成、段落标签、honors。

Rhythm and groove as musical material (节奏与律动) - what a rhythm is before anyone plays it. Beat feel versus tempo as independent variables, the weight structure of the bar, syncopation and anticipation and the precondition both require, the three ingredients of groove, onbeat versus offbeat feel and bounce, the melody's three possible relationships with the backbeat, and the ways a rhythmic figure can be repeated, displaced, deformed and contrasted. Use when choosing a beat feel or tempo, when a groove is stiff or foursquare, when the melody and the rhythm pattern are fighting, when deciding where accents fall, or when a section needs rhythmic contrast. 节奏、律动、拍子、切分、先现、八beat、十六beat、shuffle、正拍反拍、hemiola。

Rhythm section arranging and MIDI programming (节奏组与打ち込み) - drums, bass and harmony instruments as one unit, and how to make programmed parts sound played. Includes a style-by-style drum pattern and tempo lookup (rock, funk, R&B, hip hop, jazz, blues, Afro-Cuban, Brazilian, country, metal, techno); kick/snare/cymbal roles, tempo ranges, straight/swing/shuffle/half-time feel, signature fills and hi-hat handling; groove classification by feel and subdivision; the order in which to pick a pattern; partial and percentage quantization; push/pull with real magnitudes; linear drumming; ghost notes; the top/bottom/left/right map of a kit; and the three ways a bass sits against the kick (locked / answering / interlocking). Use when choosing a drum pattern or tempo for a style, when programmed drums sound mechanical, when deciding what to quantize, or when filling the tempo/groove/push_pull/fill_policy/bass_kick_relation fields of an ARR-SPEC. 节奏组、各风格鼓型、速度区间、groove 分类、贝司、打ち込み、量化、律动、幽灵音符、线性鼓、抢拍拖拍、过门。

Synth and timbre design as an arrangement decision (音色设计) - deciding what a sound must be before touching a knob. The four-question intent checklist (percussive or pitched / register / envelope shape / bright or dark) and its mapping to oscillator, tune, amp EG and filter; resetting to an unprocessed starting state instead of browsing presets; the sculpting model of subtractive synthesis; filter selection; and why a pure sine bass vanishes on small speakers (difference tones). Use when choosing or designing a patch, when a synth sound is generic or preset-sounding, when a bass disappears on phones or laptops, when a pad has no character, or when writing the timbre descriptors of an ARR-SPEC roster. 音色设计、合成器、滤波器、波封、预设、贝斯消失、差音。

Mandarin and Cantonese pop as a style layer (华语流行风格层). What is actually specific to Chinese-language pop rather than borrowed wholesale from J-pop and Anglo-American pop, the transfer table for what may and may not be carried in or out, the tone-melody constraint that shapes Mandarin and Cantonese melody writing and why judging it belongs to the lyricist, what the corpus can currently support and what it cannot, and the declared gaps. Use when writing or arranging Mandarin or Cantonese pop, when deciding whether a J-pop or Western device fits, when a melody fights the words, or when choosing references. 华语流行、中文流行、国语、粤语、倒字、协音、华语编曲。

Cinematic and hybrid orchestral music as a style layer (影视管弦与 hybrid 风格层) - the library's landing point for what "film grade" actually means. The three colour-configuration principles (pure-timbre layering, juxtaposition, and the mixed use of both), unison-that-is-not-unison and rhythmic heterophony as tension devices, why cinematic harmony is often non-functional and what replaces function, the orchestral-plus-electronic hybrid stack, the difference between scoring to picture and writing a song, and the transfer table. Use when writing orchestral or hybrid cues, when a track needs scale rather than volume, when an orchestral mockup sounds fake, or when borrowing cinematic devices into song-form music. 影视配乐、管弦、hybrid、氛围、电影级、trailer、齐奏不齐。

City pop and R&B as a style layer (都会流行与 R&B 风格层) - the sound built on borrowed jazz harmony, a pushed bass, and deliberate space. The harmonic vocabulary that defines it and where it comes from, the rhythm-section signature of a bass ahead of the grid against drums on it, the instrumentation roster with its register discipline, a measured spectrum budget, why R&B is the most subtractive style in the corpus, and the transfer table. Use when writing or arranging city pop, neo-soul, or R&B-adjacent pop, when a track needs that late-night urban sound, when a groove needs to lean forward, or when borrowing these devices elsewhere. 都会流行、city pop、R&B、neo-soul、丸サ进行、抢拍贝司、Rhodes。

EDM and club music as a style layer (电子舞曲风格层) - a form built on layer addition and subtraction rather than verses and choruses. Why club structure works on the floor and not at home, the long build and the drums-only section that exists for the DJ, layering as form when there is no melody to carry it, the one place where absolute quantization is correct and the one constraint that still applies, sound design as the primary compositional act in this style, and the transfer table. Use when writing or arranging EDM, house, techno or club-oriented tracks, when a build does not build, when a drop lands flat, or when borrowing club devices into song-form music. 电子舞曲、EDM、house、techno、四踩、drop、build、层叠、俱乐部。

Hip-hop and trap as a style layer (嘻哈风格层); beat-first music where the producer is a programmer, not a drummer. Covers the third time-feel from Dilla Time (straight and swung at once) with usable numbers (rushed snare ~65 ms, per-voice swing, shift-timing ticks), the tempo bands for standard / slow / half-time, the 808 as harmony carrier versus the kick, sample-based beat making from Schloss's Making Beats (digging, looping vs chopping, sampling ethics, locking up a beat, sample layers in the roster), and rap vocals from How to Rap 1 & 2 (flow on the grid, rests and breath, delivery dimensions of pitch / volume / timbre / staccato, 16-bar verse and 4- or 8-bar hook, ad-libs, the rap-versus-sung boundary). Use when writing or arranging hip-hop, trap, boom-bap, lo-fi or a rap section inside another style, when a beat sounds stiff, when the 808 fights the kick, or when deciding what to sample and how to chop it. 嘻哈、说唱、trap、boom bap、808、Dilla、半拍、律动、beat、采样、切片、chop、loop、digging、flow、delivery、气口、ad-lib。

Jazz as a style layer (爵士风格层) - what is specific to jazz and what is merely general music theory wearing a jazz hat. Chord-scale theory and the avoid-note idea, melodic minor harmony and the interchangeability that makes altered dominants work, the diminished and whole-tone resources, comping and voicing conventions, the head-solos-head form, bebop phrasing and accent placement, what a jazz arrangement measurably does differently (smallest roster, fewest entry events in the corpus), and an explicit transfer table saying which of these survive outside jazz. Use when writing or arranging in a jazz idiom, when a progression needs jazz reharmonization, when comping, when adding a solo section, or when deciding whether a jazz device belongs in a pop track. 爵士、bebop、和弦音阶、变化属、二五一、swing、solo、comping。

J-pop as a style layer (日式流行风格层) - the chorus-centred design discipline that distinguishes Japanese pop from Western pop. Why the sabi sounds like the sabi and the first-aid kit when it will not lift, the two maximization strategies (exposure and anticipation) and the boredom trade-off that governs them, the internal structure of a chorus and the two ways to build one, the role and the optional nature of the o-sabi, the B-melo as a genuinely Japanese invention, and the transfer table for what survives outside J-pop. Use when writing or arranging J-pop or anime-adjacent pop, when a chorus does not lift, when deciding whether to add a bridge, or when borrowing a J-pop device into another style. 日式流行、Jpop、サビ、副歌、B メロ、大サビ、落ちサビ、动漫歌。

Latin as a style layer (拉丁风格层) - three families that must never be blended into one "Latin" setting; Afro-Cuban, Brazilian and Caribbean. The clave system as the grammar that decides son or rumba and 2-3 or 3-2, the division of labour between conga tumbao, bass tumbao, piano montuno and timbale cascara and which of them actually holds the grid, where the lightness of bossa comes from and why samba never settles, the percussion roster with its register discipline, and a transfer table. Use when writing or arranging salsa, mambo, cha cha, songo, samba, bossa nova, baiao, batucada, reggae, ska or latin rock, when a pop track needs a Latin percussion layer, or when deciding whether a clave-based device belongs in another style. 拉丁、clave、Afro-Cuban、salsa、mambo、cha cha、songo、samba、bossa nova、baiao、reggae、tumbao、montuno、cascara。

Rock and band-format music as a style layer (乐队编制风格层) - what changes when five people in a room have to play it. The band roster as a hard constraint, why rock opens with fewer instruments than any other style, power chords and the harmony rules that stop applying, and riff as the primary hook carrier - Rooksby's 30 riff types (interval / scale / chord based), riff length and the 3+1 repetition pattern, riff vs vocal (alternate, end-of-line, or sustain), where riffs sit in the form, variation devices, riff-drum-bass dovetailing, twin-guitar roles, drop D / open G tuning, and the transfer table. Use when arranging for a band lineup, when a track needs a riff hook, when a riff sounds monotonous or fights the vocal, when a rock arrangement feels thin or muddy, or when borrowing band devices into produced music. 摇滚、乐队、band、riff 写作、riff 类型、power chord、失真吉他、双吉他、drop D、调弦、现场感。

Compiling ARR-SPEC into symbolic notation (符号乐谱输出) - ABC, MusicXML and MIDI from one emitter. Why the symbolic path matters (it is the only fully reproducible output and the only way YuE2 executes rather than guesses), the field-by-field mapping from spec to ABC headers and body, roman numerals to letter chords, multi-voice and per-part output, what each target format can and cannot carry, MIDI CC and velocity for expression, and the verification loop that catches a bad emit before it reaches a synth. Use when producing ABC for YuE2, when exporting MIDI or MusicXML for a DAW, when a deterministic reference render is needed for A/B, or when an LLM should write notation directly. 符号乐谱、ABC、MusicXML、MIDI、打ち込み、直出乐谱、确定性渲染。

Texture and spectral layering (织体与频谱分层) - arranging as a space budget rather than an instrument list. Foreground/middle-ground/background depth planning, the perceptual cues that decide what a listener hears as lead, rate-of-change discipline per depth layer, the frequency budget and the three ways to resolve a collision (yield / separate registers / alternate), and the maximal-density method for building dense sections. Use when a mix or arrangement sounds muddy, flat, or two-dimensional, when two parts fight, when the wrong element is grabbing attention, when something is written but inaudible, or when filling the spectrum_budget field of an ARR-SPEC. Grounded in critical bands, masking asymmetry (low masks high), temporal masking and auditory grouping. 织体、频段预算、临界频带、掩蔽、前中后景、深度、密度、声部打架。

Vocal direction and harmony design (演唱指导与和声设计) - specifying how a vocal should be delivered, not just what notes it sings. The two musical criteria, the vocabulary that actually changes a performance (brighter rather than louder, harder consonants rather than louder), consonant/vowel separation and why the beat lives in the vowel, the anti-perfection pitch philosophy that keeps a vocal from sounding machine-made, the four harmony types with their purpose and delivery, double and triple panning, and how all of this maps onto text prompts for Suno / YuE2 / MiniMax. Use when a vocal sounds flat, machine-made, or buried, when planning harmonies or doubles, when writing the vocal block of an ARR-SPEC, or when a generated vocal is too perfectly in tune. 演唱、人声、和声、咬字、音准、双轨、AI 味。

Entry point and router for the music composition library (作曲编曲工作流与路由). The S0-S7 stage table from brief to delivered audio, which skill to load for which task, the full-library boundary table that prevents two skills claiming the same decision, the ARR-SPEC gate rules, and the three checks (boundary tables against style bleed, text-layer A/B, compliance rate). Load this FIRST for any request that will produce or change an ARR-SPEC (a whole track, a section rewrite, a generation run). A single knowledge question or a single-part task goes straight to the owning skill without this one. Use when starting a new track, when unsure which skill owns a question, when a spec fails lint, when a generated result sounds wrong and you need the diagnostic path, or when handing the spec to another department (lyrics, mixing, editing). 作曲、编曲、工作流、路由、该读哪个 skill、ARR-SPEC、出歌流程。
